title: The many Loyacanos, Mike Lalla and Bourbon Street players
summary: His wife explains unrelated Loyacano musicians; talk moves to Mike Lalla, Bourbon Street groups and the Confederate colonels.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: That's right. He's a good man. He played with the Lloyd Canada, Steve and and Joe and the other one. What were the other boys? Freddie. Freddie. He played with them. Well are you all related? No, no relation with it at all. All Lloyd Canada, no relations? No relations at all. All played together and had a bit of relations.
You practically had your nothing but Lloyd Canada's in the band. That's right, that's right. What would you do with a 50-piece jazz band? Oh god. I don't believe you'd be able to play

blocks.x: jazz with 50 men. No, I think and you played, I don't know if you played with Mike Lalla, did you?
Yeah, sure Mike Lalla. Black Mike too. Well that's quite a, that's quite a long way between Mike and Black Mike.
Yeah, you ain't kidding. Mike's working at Doha now. He is? Relief, relief band. Oh yeah.

Who that's Roy still down there? Somebody told me Roy went with Roy, Roberto. Yeah? Yeah, they had a real uh... Push out, huh? Yeah. All Bourbon Street has changed now recently. Yeah, I guess so. Mark went with Roy, Roberto, Bob Coquille. Oh yeah, Bob went with him.
